about.title: Personal Injury Help in Calistoga, California
about.longDescription: Calistoga is a small city, but its roads carry a steady mix of local traffic, visitors headed to the valley, and vehicles moving through on Rt 29. Public records show 13 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, with 16 people hurt, and reports tend to bunch up on Friday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. — likely tied to weekend travel patterns along corridors like Foothill Boulevard, Rt 128, and Lincoln Avenue. If you were injured in one of these crashes, or in any kind of accident around town, you probably have questions about medical bills, insurance calls, and what happens next. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Calistoga with an independent personal injury attorney — we are not a law firm, and we don't provide legal advice ourselves. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover money. Our goal is simply to help you find someone who can look at your situation, explain your options under California law, and help you move forward without guessing alone.

whyChoose.title: Why Connect With an Attorney Through LawProactive

items.title: The clock is running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting to talk to someone can cost you options.

items.title: Shared fault doesn't shut you out
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for what happened — your share of fault simply reduces the amount, it doesn't eliminate it.

items.title: No cap on your pain and suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California doesn't limit the amount of non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, that a person can recover.

items.title: You don't pay unless there's a recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to have your case reviewed and no fee unless money is recovered on your behalf.

items.question: Do I have to pay anything to get connected with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover money for you.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent personal injury attorneys. We don't provide legal representation or advice ourselves.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an injury in Calistoga?
items.answer: In most California personal injury cases, you have two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If your claim involves a government entity, the deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do injury crashes tend to cluster in Calistoga?
items.answer: Based on public crash records, reported injury collisions in Calistoga are associated with corridors including Rt 29, Foothill Boulevard, Rt 128, and Lincoln Avenue, with more reports occurring on Fridays between roughly 4 and 6 p.m. These are neutral collision counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility for the accident. Your total recovery would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't automatically barred.
